name: B47ANCE’d Provisions

features.text: Original dried-apple art: transparent inventory master/64x64 export plus locally authored three-slice Blender model with varied shapes, curled edges, irregular creases, single albedo atlas, FBX and preview. Offline topology, separated surfaces and round-trip checked; per-item runtime icon/model hookup pending.

Server-owned in-place apple drying in native racks: same ID/nutrients, carried age, private server ledger and copied item snapshots, saved settings, exact actor/item/access checks, carried-batch recovery and full-item resource sync. Offline only.

Client-only apple/rack drying prechecks with localized failed/unknown states, bounded user-triggered scans and sandbox display toggle. Never starts drying or proves whole-item eligibility; native SP/dedicated not tested.
Read-only vanilla food/freshness/nutrition/preservation inspection, ingredient registry and optional inventory report.
Engine-independent preservation state machine and optional appliance water/power reservation coordinator; no native production process registered.

Distinct dried-food item/native recipe and broader preservation processes remain planned. The first implemented alternative retains Base.Apple identity and uses its own server timer without a native craft.

Native Lua dispatch, save/load/auto-rot under interrupted conversion, transfer crash ordering, station destruction, late join/rejoin, dedicated contention/restart and stable-release validation remain untested. Original native-recipe route is still blocked.

limits: Native SP/dedicated NOT TESTED; G7/stable G8 BLOCKED. Dried result keeps Base.Apple identity and vanilla appearance. Loaded sampled time only; unloaded/long gaps pause. Native transfer crash atomicity is not claimed. No package/deploy/publication. Legacy identifiers retained.

relations.text: Existing appliance reservation contract; legacy global and paired-build compatibility unverified. Fruit drying has no power dependency.
Existing appliance fluid reservation contract; no production process. Fruit drying has no water dependency.
